problem: The exchange stops at Access-Accept and 'Port open'. The final EAP message of the standard flow is missing: the authenticator sends EAP-Success to the supplicant after Access-Accept (and EAP-Failure after Access-Reject). The figure label 'Identity?' also hides the real frame name, EAP-Request/Identity.
fix: Add a last step: after Access-Accept, the switch sends EAP-Success to the supplicant and only then forwards normal traffic; after Access-Reject it sends EAP-Failure. Label the second message 'EAP-Request/Identity'.

problem: 'normal traffic on that port belongs to zero VLANs' can be read as if the port has no VLAN configured at all. Strictly, the port simply is not authorized to forward data traffic in any VLAN; in some deployments it is parked in a restricted guest VLAN.
fix: Say: before authentication the port forwards no normal data in any VLAN (0 normal-traffic VLANs); only EAPOL frames pass. Some deployments put an unauthorized port in a restricted guest VLAN.
